newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah lower on central bank fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah lower on central bank fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was lower against the dollar in slow late trading on Friday after the central bank raised its fixing in the afternoon, dealers said.
The central bank surprised the market by raising its intervention band by one point to 2,326/2,518, taking the total raising in this week to three points.
"This seems to have surprised the market somehow. The rate was adjusted but I don't think the central bank had absorbed many dollars from the market," one local bank dealer said.
He said trading was slow, but the move could trigger some shifting of market perceptions of the dollar-rupiah trend.
The local bank dealer said the three-point depreciation in the week could reduce operators' interest of holding short dollars and help the dollar rebound after recent pressure.
"The risk-reward scenario seems to favour long dollar holding if the central bank continues to depreciate the rupiah by three points a week," he said.
"It's not worth much to extend short dollar positions if overnight costs average around 0.43 points," he added.
"I think there could be some shifting in favour of dollars if the central bank maintains its fixing policy."
Spot rupiah was last at 2,326.0/26.2 at 0930 GMT against an opening of 2,325.50/26.25 at the opening. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,325.3/25.6 and 2,324.35/24.60, respectively.
Overnight swap was at 0.90/0.95 and tom/next at 0.48/0.55.
Dealers said longer-term swaps were relatively stable.
One-month swap was at 17.00/17.50, two at 33.5/34,5, three at 50.25/50.50 and six at 98.00/99.25 points.
The central bank also raised its the conversion rate by one point to 2,326/2,374 on Friday.
